children: Basis bids for corn shipped by barge to the US Gulf Coast declined on Thursday as exporter demand for the grain slowed, while soybean barge bids held steady, traders said.
Showers this week have slowed the final stages of the Midwest corn and soybean harvest.

"Fieldwork remains sluggish in the wake of recent rainfall," the US Department of Agriculture said in a weather note, adding that more than 15% of the soybeans remained in the field in several Midwestern states as of November 1, including Missouri, Michigan, Ohio and Nebraska.
However, the rains helped improve water levels on Midwest rivers, and draft restrictions were expected to ease on the Mississippi River south of Cairo, Illinois, a barge source said.
At the Gulf, CIF corn barges loaded in November were bid at 89 cents over Chicago Board of Trade December (CZ26) futures, down 4 cents from Wednesday.
FOB export premiums for Gulf corn vessels loaded in December held steady at around 110 cents over futures.
For soybeans, CIF barges loaded in November were bid at 106 cents over CBOT January soybean (SF27) futures, unchanged from Wednesday.
FOB export premiums for Gulf soybeans loaded in December were steady at about 118 cents over January futures.
The USDA reported net export sales of US soybeans in the week to October 29 at 1,456,100 metric tons, in line with trade expectations but down 11% from the prior four-week average.
The USDA reported net weekly corn sales at 1,294,600 tons, in line with expectations and up 10% from the four-week average.
Net wheat sales for the week totaled 538,000 tons, toward the high end of expectations for 300,000 to 650,000 tons and up 16% from the four-week average.
China is open to buying more US farm goods, but only if the two sides implement their reciprocal tariff-cut agreement, the commerce ministry said.
